Container.Name: tasmofleet
Container.Overview: Tasmota fleet manager: inventory, health, safe OTA updates and backups for Tasmota devices. Serves firmware to devices on plain HTTP port 80 of its own IP; the UI on port 8080 belongs behind a reverse proxy. Ports are not variables: the UI is always container port 8080, the firmware server port 80. Every variable is described in docs/configuration.md (https://github.com/nofuturekid/tasmofleet/blob/main/docs/configuration.md). Only bootstrap settings are variables here; device networks, MQTT, firmware, backups, discovery, policy and single sign-on are configured on the System settings page after the first sign-in. Emergency access (IdP down): sign in with a local admin on the normal login page; reset its password with `tasmofleet user passwd`.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Database, secret.key, firmware cache, backups. Back it up as a whole: without secret.key the stored device passwords cannot be decrypted. The container runs as UID/GID 65532 (not nobody 99:100): run 'chown -R 65532:65532 /mnt/user/appdata/tasmofleet' once if the folder is not writable.

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: External URL of the UI (OIDC redirect and logout target), e.g. https://tasmofleet.example.com. Required for AUTH_MODE=oidc.

Config.Name: Trusted proxies
Config.Description: Comma separated CIDRs of the reverse proxy. Forwarded headers and header-auth are trusted only from these peers.

Config.Name: Initial admin password
Config.Description: Password of the first local admin on a fresh install (must be changed at the first sign-in). Empty: a random one is written to initial-admin-password in the data directory.

Config.Name: Metrics token
Config.Description: Leave empty to set the scrape token on the settings page (System, Metrics); a value here locks it. Bearer token required on /metrics for remote scrapers; without any token only local scrapes are answered.

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: Leave empty to choose debug, info, warn or error on the settings page; a value here locks it. Logs are JSON on stdout.
